rationale: Sass's module system is the class this lane's GRAMMAR exists for. `@use 'sass:map' as map;` did not parse at all on the stock grammar — the rule was `seq('@use', $._value, ';')` and nothing else — and it was the largest residual class in the corpus at 277 error spans. Pinned together with `@include` because they are the two ends of one relationship: the declaration publishes a symbol, the use names it, and the edge is only meaningful if BOTH ends resolve. The `as` namespace is on the import because it is the part a consumer cannot recover from the module path: `@use 'sass:map' as map` and `@use 'sass:map' as m` are the same import and different graphs. `as *` deliberately publishes NO namespace symbol — there is no name to publish, and a symbol for the keyword `*` would be a name with no referent. The mixin keeps its keyword in its published name, for the reason `@font-face Inter` does in the CSS lane. Every relationship here also pins its LINE, and that is not decoration: the `line-numbers-dropped` mutant removes `line_number` from every edge, which changes no symbol and no edge COUNT, and it SURVIVED until these pins existed. Line provenance is the one class a counting gate cannot see, so it has to be asserted directly (M59/#855).
